investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-19T20:05–20:13Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, preventing the eval runner from reaching any assertion.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity (no lower-priority victims found), every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct reflection of this infrastructure state; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1884-1885: runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent with machineType='remote', confirming a VM-backed pod must be scheduled before any evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:254-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod is never scheduled.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption confirms no lower-priority pods are present to evict.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those rules recently became more restrictive, the effective capacity would have dropped without any code change.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the cluster is too small to absorb concurrent eval probes plus any live workload, causing transient exhaustion during the eval window.
Lower probability — node affinity selector targets a node label that was removed or changed on the 4 non-matching nodes, shrinking the eligible pool from a larger set to just 2 nodes.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T20:08–20:13Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the check produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing from the output.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent provisioning path has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the two eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no VM slot was available for any of the three eval pods. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers the pod scheduling path; because the pod remained Unschedulable for ~128–145 seconds across all three checks, the runner never reached the state-polling logic and returned no evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: remote-agent-state contract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none present because agent creation never completed
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: both nodes that carry the VM resource are fully allocated, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already small and any saturation of those 2 nodes causes total unavailability. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in all three check messages.

Tertiary — concurrent eval or production workload consuming all available VM slots on the two eligible nodes at the time of the run: a burst of real or eval-driven remote agent pods may have pre-occupied both nodes before the eval pods were submitted. No direct evidence of concurrent workload is present in the packet, so this remains a hypothesis.

Lower confidence — preemption policy preventing recovery: the scheduler message 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod' and 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling' indicate that even priority-based preemption could not free a slot, suggesting all running pods on those nodes have equal or higher priority than the eval pod.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a concurrent workload released its VM slots), not a sustained capacity deficit.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-19T20:05–20:13Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, preventing the eval runner from reaching any assertion.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity (no lower-priority victims found), every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct reflection of this infrastructure state; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck 145s, latencyMs=148967 — same infrastructure constraint hit independently.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1884-1885: runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent with machineType='remote', confirming a VM-backed pod must be scheduled before any evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:254-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod is never scheduled.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption confirms no lower-priority pods are present to evict.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those rules recently became more restrictive, the effective capacity would have dropped without any code change.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the cluster is too small to absorb concurrent eval probes plus any live workload, causing transient exhaustion during the eval window.
Lower probability — node affinity selector targets a node label that was removed or changed on the 4 non-matching nodes, shrinking the eligible pool from a larger set to just 2 nodes.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T20:08–20:13Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the check produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing from the output.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent provisioning path has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the two eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no VM slot was available for any of the three eval pods. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers the pod scheduling path; because the pod remained Unschedulable for ~128–145 seconds across all three checks, the runner never reached the state-polling logic and returned no evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: remote-agent-state contract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none present because agent creation never completed
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: both nodes that carry the VM resource are fully allocated, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already small and any saturation of those 2 nodes causes total unavailability. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in all three check messages.

Tertiary — concurrent eval or production workload consuming all available VM slots on the two eligible nodes at the time of the run: a burst of real or eval-driven remote agent pods may have pre-occupied both nodes before the eval pods were submitted. No direct evidence of concurrent workload is present in the packet, so this remains a hypothesis.

Lower confidence — preemption policy preventing recovery: the scheduler message 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod' and 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling' indicate that even priority-based preemption could not free a slot, suggesting all running pods on those nodes have equal or higher priority than the eval pod.

The eval failure is a direct consequence: the probe at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) calls createAgent with type "remote", which submits the pod that cannot be scheduled, so no agent identity or runtime response is ever produced and the expected-output contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 266-270) cannot be satisfied.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful remote-agent pod scheduling event on the same cluster at the same time would disprove kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion as the cause.

kubectl describe node output showing available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes at the time of the failure would disprove resource exhaustion and point to a different scheduling constraint.
A passing run of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime with full evidence collected would indicate the failure was transient rather than a sustained capacity problem.
Evidence that the pod's nodeAffinity/nodeSelector spec changed between a previously passing run and this run would shift the primary cause from resource exhaustion to a configuration regression.
A scheduler event showing the pod was eventually scheduled but the agent process itself failed would disprove the pod-never-started hypothesis and implicate the agent runtime instead.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on the affinity-eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent pod creation, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct signal rather than a pod scheduling timeout.

Add a node-affinity health check that verifies at least N nodes in the cluster match the remote-agent pod's nodeAffinity/nodeSelector, alerting early if the eligible node pool shrinks below a safe threshold.
Add a stale-pod cleanup eval that detects remote-agent pods stuck in Pending or Running beyond a TTL, to prevent slot leakage from prior eval runs from blocking future scheduling.

Consider adding a pre-flight scheduling dry-run step to the remote-agent-create probe that uses the Kubernetes scheduler simulation (e.g., kubectl --dry-run) to detect Unschedulable conditions before the full agent creation attempt, enabling faster and cheaper failure detection.
